cases.question: In what order does Three Colours: Blue appear in the Three Colours trilogy?
cases.before_context:
[d05p000] Blue
[d05s000] Blue is the colour between violet and green on the spectrum of visible light.
[d05s001] Human eyes perceive blue when observing light with a wavelength between 450 and 495 nanometres. Blues with a higher frequency and thus a shorter wavelength appear more violet, while those with a lower frequency and a longer wavelength gradually appear more green.
[d05s002] Pure blue, in the middle, has a wavelength of 470 nanometres.

[d04p000] Three Colours: Blue
[d04s000] Three Colours: Blue (French: Trois couleurs : Bleu ) is a 1993 French drama film directed and co-written by Polish filmmaker Krzysztof Kieślowski.
[d04s001] "Blue" is the first of three films that comprise the "Three Colours" trilogy, themed on the French Revolutionary ideals of liberty, equality, and fraternity; it is followed by "" and "".
[d04s002] According to Kieślowski, the subject of the film is liberty, specifically emotional liberty, rather than its social or political meaning.

[d06p000] Three Colours trilogy
[d06s000] The "Three Colours" trilogy (Polish: "Trzy kolory" , French: "Trois couleurs" ) is a three-part film series directed by Krzysztof Kieślowski.
[d06s001] Two of the films were made in French and one primarily in Polish: "" (1993), "" (1994), and "" (1994).
[d06s002] All three were co-written by Kieślowski and Krzysztof Piesiewicz (with story consultants Agnieszka Holland and Sławomir Idziak) and have musical scores by Zbigniew Preisner.

[d05p003] Blue
[d05s003] In painting and traditional colour theory, blue is one of the three primary colours of pigments, along with red and yellow, which can be mixed to form a wide gamut of colours.
[d05s004] Red and blue mixed together form violet, blue and yellow together form green.
[d05s005] Blue is also a primary colour in the RGB colour model, used to create all the colours on the screen of a television or computer monitor.

[d03s000] The Hokusai Manga (北斎漫画 , "Hokusai's Sketches") is a collection of sketches of various subjects by the Japanese artist Hokusai.
[d03s001] Subjects of the sketches include landscapes, flora and fauna, everyday life and the supernatural.
[d03s002] The word "manga" in the title does not refer to the contemporary story-telling "manga", as the sketches in the work are not connected to each other.

[d00s000] Three Colours: White (French: Trois couleurs : Blanc ) is a 1994 French-Polish comedy-drama film co-written, produced, and directed by Krzysztof Kieślowski.
[d00s001] "White" is the second in "The Three Colors Trilogy", themed on the French Revolutionary ideals, following "" and preceding "".
[d00s002] The film was selected as the Polish entry for the Best Foreign Language Film at the 67th Academy Awards, but was not accepted as a nominee.

[d07s000] The City of Sydney flag is made up of a horizontal triband of three colours – white, gold and blue.
[d07s001] It was designed in 1908.

[d01s003] The vinyl is available in three colours: Blue, orange and white (Hot Topic Exclusive).
[d01s004] Each colour is limited to 500.
[d01s005] The music video for the song was released through Absolute Punk on 6 August 2009.

[d02p000] Colombia (cocktail)
[d02s000] The Colombia is a cocktail containing vodka and curaçao.
[d02s001] The layering effect takes advantage of the variation in density and temperature between the layers.
[d02s002] The drink appears as stacked horizontal layers of yellow, blue and red, which matches the three colours of the Colombian flag.

[d09p000] Requiem for my friend (Preisner)
[d09s000] Requiem for my friend is a major and the first non-film musical work composed by Zbigniew Preisner.
[d09s001] The composition was meant to honour the composer's late friend, the director Krzysztof Kieślowski, with whom he collaborated while working on a number of films, including the famous "Three Colours" trilogy.
[d09s002] The album was released in 1998 although some parts of the work must have been ready upon Kieślowski's passing as Preisner asserted in an interview that "the Requiem had accompanied Krzysztof in his last journey".

cases.question: Thomas Fitch defended John Henry Holliday when he was accused of killing men during the gunfight at the o.k. corral, when was that?

[d01p000] Thomas Fitch (politician)
[d01s000] Thomas Fitch (January 27, 1838 – November 12, 1923) was an American lawyer and politician.
[d01s001] He defended President Brigham Young of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints and other church leaders when Young and his denomination were prosecuted for polygamy in 1871 and 1872.
[d01s002] He also successfully defended Virgil, Morgan, and Wyatt Earp along with Doc Holliday when they were accused of murdering Billy Clanton, and Tom and Frank McLaury during the October 25, 1881 Gunfight at the O.K. Corral.

[d03p000] Doc Holliday
[d03s000] John Henry "Doc" Holliday (August 14, 1851 – November 8, 1887) was an American gambler, gunfighter, and dentist, and a good friend of Wyatt Earp.
[d03s001] He is best known for his role as a temporary deputy marshal in the events leading up to and following the Gunfight at the O.K. Corral.

[d02p000] Hour of the Gun
[d02s000] Hour of the Gun is a 1967 Western film depicting Wyatt Earp and Doc Holliday during their 1881 battles against Ike Clanton and his brothers in the Gunfight at the O.K. Corral, and the gunfight's aftermath in and around Tombstone, Arizona, starring James Garner as Earp, Jason Robards as Holliday, and Robert Ryan as Clanton.
[d02s001] The movie was directed by John Sturges.

[d08p006] Gunfight at the O.K. Corral
[d08s006] Virgil, Morgan, and Doc Holliday were wounded, but Wyatt Earp was unharmed.
[d08s007] The shootout has come to represent a period of the American Old West when the frontier was virtually an open range for outlaws, largely unopposed by law enforcement officers who were spread thin over vast territories.

cases.question: Are The Man from Snowy River II and Miracle of the White Stallions filmed in different countries?

[d03p000] The Man from Snowy River and Other Verses
[d03s000] The Man from Snowy River and Other Verses (1895) is the first collection of poems by Australian poet Banjo Paterson.
[d03s001] It was released in hardback by Angus and Robertson in 1895, and features the poet's widely anthologised poems "The Man from Snowy River", "Clancy of the Overflow", "Saltbush Bill" and "The Man from Ironbark".
[d03s002] It also contains the poet's first two poems that featured in The Bulletin Debate, a famous dispute in "The Bulletin" magazine from 1892-93 between Paterson and Henry Lawson.

[d06s001] Released in Australia as "Banjo Paterson's The Man from Snowy River", the series was subsequently released in both the United States and the United Kingdom as "Snowy River: The McGregor Saga".

[d00p000] Return to Snowy River

[d00s001] The soundtrack album is named after the American title for the film.

[d04p000] The Man from Snowy River (poem)
[d04s000] "The Man from Snowy River" is a poem by Australian bush poet Banjo Paterson.
[d04s001] It was first published in "The Bulletin", an Australian news magazine, on 26 April 1890, and was published by Angus & Robertson in October 1895, with other poems by Paterson, in "The Man from Snowy River and Other Verses".

[d09p000] Snowy River
[d09s000] The Snowy River is a major river in south-eastern Australia.
[d09s001] It originates on the slopes of Mount Kosciuszko, Australia's highest mainland peak, draining the eastern slopes of the Snowy Mountains in New South Wales, before flowing through the Alpine National Park and the Snowy River National Park in Victoria and emptying into Bass Strait.
